facts.statement: Jiangshanosaurus was a herbivorous sauropod that lived in China between 92 and 88 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Jiangshanosaurus is a genus of herbivorous titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur that lived in China approximately 92-88 million years ago, during the Turonian and Coniacian stages of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: A sauropod skeleton was excavated in 1977 and 1978 from the Jinhua Formation in Lixian Village, Zhejiang province, China.
facts.quote: In 1977 and 1978 a sauropod skeleton was excavated by paleontologists Wei Feng, Wu Weitang and Kang Ximin in the Jinhua Formation of Lixian Village, Jiangshan county, in the eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang.

facts.statement: The species Jiangshanosaurus lixianensis was formally described by Tang Feng and colleagues in 2001.
facts.quote: The type and only named species, Jiangshanosaurus lixianensis, was formally described by Tang Feng, Kang, Jin Xingsheng, Wei and Wu in 2001.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes shoulder elements, five back vertebrae, three tail vertebrae, pubic bones, ischia, and a left femur.
facts.quote: The holotype, ZNM M1322, of J.lixianensis includes elements of the left shoulder, five back vertebrae, three tail vertebrae, the pubic bones, the ischia, and a left femur.

facts.statement: A unique trait of Jiangshanosaurus is that in specific tail vertebrae, ridges from the neural spine are placed inside the front articulation processes rather than touching them.
facts.quote: In the vertebrae positioned at the transition between the tail base and the middle tail, the lower ends of the laminae spinoprezygapophyseales, the ridges running from the neural spine towards the front articulation processes, are placed to the inside of these processes, the prezygapophyses, instead of touching them.

facts.statement: A 2019 study placed Jiangshanosaurus in the Somphospondyli in a basal position outside the Titanosauria.
facts.quote: According to the 2019 study, Jiangshanosaurus was placed in the Somphospondyli in a basal position, outside the Titanosauria.

facts.statement: While initially considered an advanced Titanosaur, recent studies suggest Jiangshanosaurus lies outside the Lithostrotia.
facts.quote: Aunque Jiangshanosaurus inicialmente se colocó comiçu un Titanosaura avanzado, un artículo reciente considera que está fuera de Lithostrotia.

facts.statement: Some sources suggest Jiangshanosaurus lived approximately 105 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 105 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The fossil record indicates Jiangshanosaurus lived from the Cenomanian to the Turonian stages, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: The shoulder structure of Jiangshanosaurus is very similar to that of Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: La estructura del hombro del Jianshanosaurus es muy similar al del Alamosaurus.

rejected.statement: The lower shaft of the ischium ends in a small hook-like process on its top outer side.
rejected.quote: The lower shaft of the ischium ends in a small process, formed as a hook, on its top outer side.

rejected.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Jiangshanosaurus to be 11 meters long and weigh 2,500 kilograms.
rejected.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at eleven meters and its weight at 2500 kg.
